title: The garment of piety
hookLine: children of Adam, We gave you clothing, but the garment of piety is best (7:26)
last: MY PRAYER — ALL OF IT FOR HIM.

cards: Surah seven is al-A'raf, the Heights, named for a scene later in it: a high wall between the garden and the fire, with people on its heights who can see both sides.
It's one of the longest Meccan surahs, and it opens by retelling a story you know: Adam, his wife, the garden and the tree.

When they eat from the tree, their nakedness becomes plain to them, and they start covering themselves with leaves from the garden. The first thing humans reached for, in this telling, was something to wear.

teach.h: LIBAS AND RISH — COVER AND FINERY.
teach.b: Right after that story, verse twenty-six turns to all of us: O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing, libas, to cover your nakedness, and rish, finery, the word for a bird's feathers.
Clothing that protects and clothing that looks good: the verse calls both a gift. Then, in Pickthall's words: “but the raiment of restraint from evil, that is best.”
In Arabic, libas at-taqwa: the garment of piety, of mindfulness of God. Commentators gave it several meanings: good character, modesty, faith, a sense of shame before doing wrong.
They agreed on the picture: an outer garment and an inner one, and the inner one is what really covers you. Libas shows up somewhere surprising, too.

teach.h: SPOUSES, A GARMENT FOR EACH OTHER.
teach.b: In surah two, about marriage, the Qur'an says spouses are a garment for each other: close, warm, covering each other's faults.

And the very next verse here, twenty-seven, warns: don't let Satan tempt you as he drew your parents out of the garden, stripping them of their garments. So clothing in this surah is never just fabric.
It's dignity, care, protection. Muslims dress in many ways, from Senegal to Indonesia, and modesty looks different from place to place. The verse doesn't settle a dress code here.
It ranks the two garments: the one you can buy is good, and the one you can't buy is best.

how: Muslims understand clothing as a gift and modesty as part of faith, though styles of dress vary widely by culture; many recite a short supplication from the hadith when putting on new clothes.

games.q: you've got two outfits for an event: one plain, one beautiful. which does 7:26 call a gift?
o: both, but the garment of piety is best.
games.why: covering and finery are both sent down as gifts; the inner garment, taqwa, is best.

practice: Feel the fabric you're wearing on your shoulders and wrists: someone made it, someone sold it, you chose it, so let that be a small thank-you.
Then ask what you're wearing on the inside today, patience or a short fuse, honesty or a little performance, and choose one quality to put on, the way you'd choose a shirt.
